[Pre-reflection] This mean-reversion strategy risks false signals during strong trending periods when prices break out of Bollinger bands, and RSI may remain oversold during sustained downtrends. The fixed stop-loss and take-profit levels based on ATR may be too rigid for varying volatility conditions, and the exit rules could lead to premature exits during strong reversals or late entries during consolidation.
[Backup plan] If results are poor, I'd test a trailing stop-loss instead of fixed TP/SL, or switch to a momentum filter (e.g., 50 EMA) to avoid entering during strong trends. If mediocre Sharpe, I'd adjust RSI threshold from 30 to 25-35 or modify BB bands from 2 to 1.5 std. As alternative, I'd try a volatility break-out strategy with dynamic entry rules using 20-period ATR and 10-period RSI for confirmation.
